themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 55 THIS WEEK, a 378% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 11.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.73), suggesting a localized or event-driven disruption affecting public spaces across East Flatbush.
evidence: 55 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
378% spike with z-score of 6.73 (statistically significant outlier)
Concurrent commercial noise complaints also elevated at 36 THIS WEEK vs. 17.5 baseline (106% increase, z-score: 4.22)
reporting_angles: Interview residents and 311 callers to identify source: construction, street vendor activity, or special events
Cross-reference with DOB permits (171 active alterations filed) to determine if construction work is driving complaints

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Disruption
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints doubled to 36 THIS WEEK compared to 17.5 weekly average (106% spike, z-score: 4.22), indicating emerging friction between businesses and residents that warrants quick investigation into what commercial activity has changed.
evidence: 36 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 17.5 weekly baseline (106% increase, z-score: 4.22)
Spike coincides with broader noise acceleration across district
303 active DOB permits including 80 new building filings suggest ongoing commercial development or renovation work
reporting_angles: Identify which commercial corridors (Flatbush Ave, Church Ave) are generating complaints
Interview business owners and residents about late-night operations, music venues, or delivery schedules

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 weekly (967% increase, z-score: 7.49), an extreme statistical anomaly suggesting either coordinated removal, storm damage aftermath, or development-related tree cutting.
evidence: 4 illegal tree damage complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
Extreme outlier suggests concentrated incident rather than gradual trend
Overlaps with active ULURP application (Constellation CB 17) in public review phase, potentially tree-removal-related
reporting_angles: Investigate whether Constellation development project or other zoned projects are clearing trees without permits
Interview Parks Department and Community Board about any recent tree removal notifications or complaints

themes_detail.label: Dumpster Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints increased to 4 LAST WEEK from 0.4 baseline (967% increase, z-score: 7.49), matching the severity of the illegal tree damage spike and potentially linked to construction activity across 303 active DOB permits.
evidence: 4 dumpster complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% increase, z-score: 7.49)
Coincides with 171 active alteration permits and 80 new building filings, suggesting construction-debris overflow
High z-score indicates extreme statistical anomaly rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Verify whether construction sites are properly managing debris and dumpster placement on public sidewalks
Interview sanitation department about enforcement actions on illegally placed or overfilled dumpsters

themes_detail.label: Uptick in For-Hire Vehicle Complaints
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, FHV services) surged to 4 THIS WEEK, a 433% increase over 0.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.92), suggesting growing congestion or double-parking issues tied to ride-hailing activity.
evidence: 4 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% increase, z-score: 3.92)
Aligns with sustained illegal parking issues (1,895 complaints over 90 days) suggesting vehicle-related pressure on streets
Potential connection to broader street/sidewalk noise spike if pickups/dropoffs are concentrated on same corridors
reporting_angles: Identify which neighborhoods or transit hubs (Jamaica Station area) are seeing most FHV congestion
Interview residents about double-parking and blocked lanes; assess whether TLC enforcement is visible
